title: Nil T2 vs Zero Return | Same Filing, Two Names

Comparison · Nil T2 Filing · Canada

Nil T2 Return vs Zero Return

Both names describe the same filing: a T2 for a tax year with no activity. What is reported as $0.00, what is not, and why the difference matters.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOWTest a Quiet Year

Quick Answer

They are the same filing. A nil return and a zero return both mean a T2 filed for a tax year in which the corporation had no revenue, no expenses, no income of any kind and no disposition of property. There is no zero-return form: the Canada Revenue Agency receives a T2 either way, at $300.00 plus HST per tax year. The word that matters is not nil or zero but the year, because the test is asked year by year and a single entry takes a year out of it.

Nil T2 filing in Canada › Nil T2 filing price › Nil T2 Return vs Zero Return

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Last reviewed: November 5, 2026

One Filing, Two Words for It

Neither nil nor zero is the name of a form. Both are ways of describing a tax year in which nothing happened, and the return that reports such a year is the ordinary T2, filed on the ordinary deadline with the schedules the corporation’s own position requires.

Every resident corporation files a T2 for every tax year, whether or not it did anything. The obligation attaches to existing as a corporation, not to earning income. The return is how the Agency learns the year was zero, and without it the year is not recorded as zero, it is recorded as missing.

So the choice of word changes nothing. What does change things is that zero activity is a statement about the twelve months rather than about the corporation: the same corporation can have a quiet year, then a trading year, then another quiet year, and each is assessed on its own.

Two rows differ. The first is the name: there is no zero-return form, and the return is the T2 either way. The second is the mistake the word zero invites, which is filing a balance sheet as entirely zero when share capital was issued. The other six rows are identical, because the two names describe one filing.

This comparison sets two of our own filing routes against each other and names no other provider. Where a comparison on this site does name one, it states that provider’s published prices and published features only.

What Is Reported as $0.00, and What Is Not

A zero-activity return is not an empty return. These are the parts that carry zeroes and the parts that do not:

  • Revenue, expenses, income of any kind and dispositions of property are reported as $0.00 for the tax year.
  • The GIFI income statement codes carry those zeroes, filed the same way a trading year files real figures.
  • Share capital issued on incorporation sits on Schedule 100 whether or not anything happened during the year.
  • A shareholder loan and retained earnings brought forward sit there too, and neither becomes zero because the year was quiet.
  • Schedule 50 still reports every shareholder at 10% or more.
  • Schedule 24 is filed on a first return, and once only.
  • Interest credited to a corporate account is investment income whatever the amount, so it takes the year out of zero activity.

A balance sheet filed as entirely zero when share capital was issued is wrong, and it is wrong in a way that persists: the next return opens from the closing balances this one reports.

The dormant corporation test settles whether a year qualifies, the nil GIFI balance sheet checker takes what Schedule 100 must carry, and the complete guide to zero-activity corporate tax returns sets out the whole subject.

A corporation with share capital on its books and nothing else in the tax year

Its income statement codes are all $0.00, and its balance sheet is not: the share capital issued on incorporation sits on Schedule 100, and so do any shareholder loan and the retained earnings brought forward. The return is a nil T2 at $300.00 plus HST per tax year, whichever of the two names brought the directors to it. Filing it as an entirely zero balance sheet would be wrong, and the error would carry into the next year, because that return opens from the closing balances this one reports. Frequently Asked Questions

Is a zero return the same as a nil T2?

Yes. Both describe a T2 filed for a tax year with no revenue, no expenses, no income of any kind and no disposition of property.

Is there a separate zero-return form?

No. The Canada Revenue Agency receives a T2 for the tax year either way. Neither nil nor zero is the name of a form.

Does the fee differ between the two?

No. There is one filing, so there is one fee: $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Does a zero-activity corporation have to file at all?

Yes. Every resident corporation files a T2 for every tax year, whether or not it did anything. The obligation attaches to existing as a corporation, not to earning income.

What happens if the year is simply not filed?

The year is not recorded as zero, it is recorded as missing. The return is how the Agency learns the year was empty.

Is the whole return filed as zeroes?

No. The income statement codes carry zeroes, but the balance sheet carries share capital, any shareholder loan and retained earnings brought forward.

Why is the balance sheet not zero if nothing happened?

Because those balances were there before the year started and are still there after it ends. A quiet year does not clear them.

What goes wrong if I file it all as zero?

The error persists. The next return opens from the closing balances this one reports, so a wrong closing balance becomes a wrong opening balance.

Does Schedule 50 still have to be filed?

Yes, for every shareholder at 10% or more. A quiet year does not change who owns the corporation.

What takes a year out of zero activity?

Any revenue, any expense, income of any kind or a disposition of property. The amount is irrelevant to the test.

Does a few dollars of bank interest count?

Yes. Interest credited to a corporate account is investment income whatever the amount, and a few dollars answers the question the same way a few thousand would.

Is zero activity decided once for the corporation?

No. It is a statement about the tax year. The same corporation can have a quiet year, then a trading year, then another quiet year.

Can several zero-activity years be filed together?

Yes. Each is its own return on its own form for its own tax year, prepared oldest first so the closing balances of one open the next, at $300.00 plus HST per tax year each.

Can a zero-activity year use the T2 Short?

Commonly, where the corporation meets the conditions. Meeting them is not automatic, and the conditions are the same under either name.

Which tool should I run first?

The dormant corporation test, which asks the six questions that settle whether the year qualifies.
